action: Mobile operators: deploy GTP-C and GTP-U security aligned with SS7 and Diameter firewalls, treat the IPX interface as untrusted, and monitor internal signalling, not only the edge. High-risk users: avoid SMS login codes.
exec: Phone networks themselves were compromised, so calls and SMS codes can be intercepted without touching the handset.
plain: Telecom security firm Enea says one hacking group took over parts of Asian phone networks to intercept calls and texts, mostly of people in Taiwan, while a second group hid spying tools inside operators' data links.

key_findings: SilentAir ran attacks from compromised SS7 and Diameter nodes inside operators in at least six Asian countries, reaching a dozen more countries with Taiwan the main target.
It redirects subscribers' location registration to intercept calls and SMS, with one-time codes seen arriving right after interception; some targets were political and government VIPs.
Enea assesses with high confidence that SilentAir is a state-level actor and, at low confidence, China-aligned; it works a UTC+8 pattern and avoids Chinese networks.
LIMINAL PANDA uses GTPDoor implants, including a new variant hiding commands in GTP-U traffic, for covert control and exfiltration tunnels between infected operators.
Enea saw several hundred covert command attempts since Q1 2026 and at least 5 to 10 infected operators, possibly several dozen worldwide.
recommendations: Deploy GTP-C and GTP-U security and align it with SS7 and Diameter firewalls for cross-protocol visibility.
Treat the IPX interface as untrusted and inspect all traffic more deeply.
Monitor internal signalling protocols and tools, not just the network edge.
Integrate signalling security with IT security and reconsider outsourcing of core networks.

summary: Enea describes two actors inside mobile networks. SilentAir, assessed as state-level, used compromised SS7 and Diameter nodes in at least six Asian countries to redirect and intercept calls and texts, mainly of Taiwanese subscribers, including one-time codes. LIMINAL PANDA used GTPDoor implants for covert command traffic and data theft between operators; Enea saw at least 5 to 10 infected operators. A link between the two is unconfirmed.
title: SilentAir and LIMINAL PANDA exploit mobile networks to spy on subscribers

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Enea report.

review.note: Compared with Enea report: six Asian countries, Taiwan, high/low confidence, GTPDoor, 5-10 operators, link unconfirmed; summary names Enea as attributing
